speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether the Ministry will consider normalising work-from-home arrangements in the post-pandemic period and advocate among companies for more flexibility in work arrangements beyond the current crisis.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Work-from-home, or WFH, has become the norm during the COVID-19 period, with many employers implementing WFH arrangements, for the safety of their employees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We are heartened by the speed at which companies and employees have adapted to the WFH arrangements during this period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Even as more are allowed to return to the workplace, some employers continue to allow their employees to WFH and return to the office only when needed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It is an encouraging sign that more people recognise the benefits of working from home and that it is becoming part of the “new normal”.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: At the same time, we recognise that WFH may not be feasible under certain conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: These include situations where workers have to be physically present at the workplace to operate machinery, or where there are challenges in working from home due to not so conducive home environments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: MOM welcomes suggestions to implement FWAs and will continue to share good practices with employers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: My question is, while working at home, many employees are subjected to really long hours.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Will MOM come up with some law to protect employees?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: We have seen people who have back-to-back meetings on Zoom and the meetings run past their lunch and dinner times.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I ask the Minister of State, out of the 85% of the companies that are offering FWAs, how many percent are actually offering WFH arrangements?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, can I also ask what was the Ministry's consideration when we so drastically reduced our WFH policy from 100% to 50%?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Why do we not just have a set of conditions or criteria where, if an employee is required to go back to work, then, they go back to work; rather than halve it quite immediately?

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: But we do know that prior to COVID-19, before the circuit breaker, there were fewer companies that were implementing WFH arrangements.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: During the circuit breaker, because of safety reasons, many companies, employers, have adapted very fast.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: We see that there is feedback from more employers telling us that they are prepared to continue to implement WFH post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I would also like to enquire, has MOM considered the downstream impact of WFH?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: With companies intending to downsize their office spaces to benefit from WFH, can we also take a look at how it impacts the downstream workers – those who are supporting office operations, such as the cleaners in the office, the food providers around the office space.

speaker: Ms Gan Siow Huang
text: As I have said earlier on, we are looking at having deeper discussions at the tripartite level to make sure that we understand the considerations fully and more holistically before we make further recommendations on implementing WFH further.
